sections.title: 5.1 What Governs Image Generation: the AR Transformer or the FM Head?
5.2 Tokenizer Is the Key to Image Generation

abstract_sentences.text: Prevailing autoregressive (AR) models for text-to-image generation either rely on heavy, computationally-intensive diffusion models to process continuous image tokens, or employ vector quantization (VQ) to obtain discrete tokens with quantization loss.

evidence.anchor: heavy, computationally-intensive diffusion models; vector quantization (VQ)

abstract_sentences.text: In this paper, we push the autoregressive paradigm forward with NextStep-1, a 14B autoregressive model paired with a 157M flow matching head, trained on discrete text tokens and continuous image tokens with next-token prediction objectives.

evidence.anchor: a 14B autoregressive model paired with a 157M flow matching head

abstract_sentences.text: NextStep-1 achieves state-of-the-art performance for autoregressive models in text-to-image generation tasks, exhibiting strong capabilities in high-fidelity image synthesis.

evidence.anchor: state-of-the-art performance for autoregressive models

abstract_sentences.text: Furthermore, our method shows strong performance in image editing, highlighting the power and versatility of our unified approach.

evidence.anchor: strong performance in image editing

abstract_sentences.text: To facilitate open research, we have released our code and models to the community at https://github.com/stepfun-ai/NextStep-1.

evidence.anchor: released our code and models to the community

introduction_moves.move: context: diffusion is dominant for high-fidelity synthesis; decoupled T5/CLIP to MMDiT fixes context and weakens multimodal fusion

evidence.anchor: This non-end-to-end design imposes rigid constraints

introduction_moves.move: problem + failure_of_prior_work: discrete AR uses VQ, introducing information bottleneck, reconstruction artifacts, exposure bias, and long sequences at low compression
introduction_moves.previous_question: why not use a unified AR model

evidence.anchor: This process introduces an information bottleneck

introduction_moves.move: failure_of_prior_work: Transfusion and Bagel process noisy inputs with clean conditions in bidirectional blocks, duplicating data and increasing sequence and attention cost
introduction_moves.previous_question: whether hybrid routes recover quality efficiently

evidence.anchor: This data duplication significantly increases the sequence length

introduction_moves.move: problem to missing_insight: continuous autoregression bypasses quantization but the performance gap remains; the paper locates the gap in image representation
introduction_moves.previous_question: can continuous AR match diffusion while retaining a standard LLM

evidence.anchor: the key to closing the performance gap lies in the image representation

introduction_moves.move: core_idea + method_preview: a well-dispersed and normalized latent space enables stable high-dimensional continuous latents with a simple causal transformer and lightweight FM head
introduction_moves.previous_question: how to repair the representation bottleneck
introduction_moves.next_hook: Section A examples and contribution list

evidence.anchor: well-dispersed and normalized latent space

related_work_moves.move: taxonomy + limitation_of_prior: diffusion/flow matching progresses from U-Net to DiT and Flow Matching, but separate text encoders impose fixed context and whole-image bidirectional cost

related_work_moves.move: taxonomy + gap_creation: discrete autoregressive models unify vision-language sequences but VQ causes information loss and limits reconstruction upper bound

related_work_moves.move: nearest_neighbor_contrast + credit_or_foundation: hybrid LLM-diffusion or noisy/clean integrated methods trade away pure causality; NextStep-1 uses strict causal continuous tokens and a lightweight head

evidence.anchor: NextStep-1 adheres to a strict causal autoregressive objective

final_judgment.single_storyline: Continuous-token AR underperforms when its latent space is poorly conditioned; NextStep-1 addresses this representation bottleneck with token-wise normalization and noise perturbation, lets a causal 14B transformer model the next-token context, and uses a lightweight patch-wise FM head to decode each continuous patch.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: Eq.1-4, Figure 1, Table 1, T2I/editing Tables 2-3, FM-head Tables 4-5, CFG Figure 3, tokenizer Figure 4, and reconstruction Table 6 are the decision-critical chain.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: OneIG/WISE results, data quantities and pipelines, Algorithm 1, latent histograms, failure cases, latency, high-resolution/SFT limitations, and LLM-use disclosure are moved to Appendix A-E.
final_judgment.best_pattern: The strongest pattern pairs an explicit representation intervention with an intermediate token-statistics diagnostic (Figure 3), a capacity control (Table 5), and a reconstruction comparison (Table 6) before making the architecture claim.
final_judgment.largest_gap: The AR-SOTA wording is not uniformly supported by Table 2, and the FM-head attribution rests on a head-only 10K-step ablation; raw/rewrite protocols, fine-tuned editing variants and absent uncertainty further narrow the claims.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a representation-to-quality claim, report the representation intervention, intermediate mechanism, same-protocol outcome and failure/cost boundary together, with model variant, prompt protocol, denominator and seed in each table.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule transfers to multimodal and latent-generation papers with component mechanisms and benchmark comparisons; theorem-only papers need formal assumptions and proof correspondences instead of benchmark controls.
final_judgment.evidence_basis: PDF p.2-p.9 main chain and p.17-p.23 appendix evidence; all claims are bounded by the cited layouts and reported protocols.
